claims.text: The starting material is single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a compositionally matched high-entropy derivative.
The baseline coercivity is approximately 100 Oe for conventionally processed single-phase fcc FeCoNi or its high-entropy derivative.
Arc melting on a water-cooled copper hearth constitutes a rapid-quenching processing route.
Rapid quenching on a water-cooled copper hearth will form a secondary C14 Laves phase in the compositionally matched alloy.
The resulting C14 Laves phase will occur as nanoscale precipitates within the fcc matrix.
The secondary C14 phase creates additional microstructural heterogeneities.
The C14-phase heterogeneities act as magnetic domain-wall pinning centers.
Pinning by the C14 phase inhibits domain-wall motion.
Rapidly quenched samples will have markedly greater coercivity than compositionally matched slow-cooled controls.
The coercivity increase could exceed one order of magnitude relative to a control with coercivity of approximately 100 Oe.
The coercivity increase may occur while high saturation magnetization is preserved.
Any observed difference between the rapid-quenching and slow-cooling groups can be isolated to processing if composition and magnetic measurement conditions are held constant.
XRD and TEM can test for the presence and microstructure of the proposed C14 phase.
VSM hysteresis measurements can compare coercivity and saturation magnetization between the rapid-quenching and slow-cooling groups.
